svg.title: Future multi-subscription quota architecture, not currently deployed
svg.desc: The same Entra tenant has subscriptions A and B with separately approved model quota. Regional Agents route to nearby same-model resources across either subscription before optional approved model fallback. Managed identity receives OpenAI User on each resource. Shared global inference capacity and tenant-wide usage-tier latency remain correlated. Multi-subscription execution is deferred.
svg.text: FUTURE REFERENCE | multiple subscriptions in the same Entra tenant
Deferred: no extra subscription provisioning, permission requests or live multi-subscription tests in the current scope.
KR / UK / US / CA / future EU
Nearby edge + regional Agents
Model-aware router / regional gateway
Same-model nearby candidates, then approved model fallback; no replay after first text
Managed Identity: Cognitive Services OpenAI User on each target resource
Subscription A | approved quota A
Subscription B | approved quota B
Global Standard, pinned model versions
Same models/versions; independent quota approval
Example consolidated pool key:
subscription A + model + version + GlobalStandard
Example consolidated pool key:
subscription B + model + version + GlobalStandard
Verify actual quota Scope and available capacity.
Contributor alone is not Entra inference permission.
Regional Scope still applies to non-onboarded models.
Role assignment requires a target-scope administrator.
Shared Microsoft-managed global inference capacity
More approved quota is not capacity isolation, reserved throughput or guaranteed lower TTFT.
Usage-tier latency guidance may aggregate all subscriptions and regions per model within a tenant.
Keep per-subscription cost controls, fairness, audit, data-governance rules and bounded retry budgets.
